George Mangos has shown extreme abilities to finish fights, especially in his last rematch performance against Justin Van Heerden. He is currently ranked #1 P4P in AusNZ and he basically has smushed everyone he's fought on the aussie regional scene. Mangos is hungry and looking for a way to get back on track with the UFC and he showed in that last fight he wanted to prove a point. I expect the same outcome for him.

posts.author: AyyLmaonnaise
posts.content:
[Predictions]

Rongzhu vs Martinez
Rongzhu KO RD 1

Pointless fight for Rongzhu but this is a hysterical matchup; I’m really shocked Martinez signed this fight and I’ll honestly be shocked if he even shows up. It’s so funny Rongzhu went from a really tough fight in enemy territory to a complete layup in China against one of the bottom 10 worst guys on the roster. I’m really high on Rongzhu as it is, and I think he is going to level up being at CKB full time. He is already leagues above Martinez so I don’t see how he loses this fight. Martinez is going to strike with him, has no power, is extremely hittable, and super chinny. Martinez does have crazy output and conditioning but he doesn’t do anything with it; he’s just a fat brawler who sits in the pocket and exists. He’s not even a real fighter either, he’s had a 15 year MMA career yet only 20 fights, and this is now his third fight in nearly 5 years with the UFC. He is a fat FW who doesn’t want to cut, and even in his wins he usually gets beat up early before winning due to his opponents gassing themselves out form beating him up. At the UFC level he has looked atrocious. I guess he did drop Tom Nolan but he got ko’ed shortly thereafter and also had that pathetic KO loss to Leavitt. I am skeptical that Martinez is going to fly to China to get taxed 50% of his purse and take a KO 1, but if he does show up I expect this to be a vicious beatdown. These two are not on the same skill level and Martinez is not a real fighter either.

Bin vs Cahyadi
Bin KO RD 1

The showcase bouts are always exciting because the UFC usually chooses good talent/guys they normally would never look at, but this fight blows. Idk why they love Bin so much, they are doing everything in their power to sign him. This is now his 4th opportunity at a ufc contract, the UFC has tried to sign him since he got released from ONE. In all fairness, he did get robbed on dwcs/last time on RTU, but it’s also his fault because he just does nothing in his fights. He’s supposed to be a grappler but instead chooses to strike now. His striking is pretty mediocre. He has okay technique but he doesn’t throw a lot and doesn’t have a ton of power either. He has bad defense as well and has been cracked many times. He got flatlined against a terrible striker in Kawana and almost died against Hwende in r3 for this as well. Bin is an okay grappler but he can easily be taken down/subbed by better guys. I won’t lie, I did not tape his opponent but like, do you really need to? Indonesians are without a doubt the worst MMA scene in the world; they have hardly any real MMA training and some of the worst grappling you’ll ever see. I don’t need to watch Yudi’s fights to know he’s a jobber. All Bin has to do is get one td and the fight is over here. He could honestly KO this guy early if he wants, especially since he loves to strike now. This is a layup so they can finally justify signing Bin. Idk why they want him so badly but if he fumbles this he should just retire

Mangos vs Yanagawa
Mangos KO RD 2

This is a really sick matchup, these two are both really good. Again, I don’t like putting Aussie fighters on RTU but for Mangos I actually don’t mind it. He’s only 22 and still very green, so fighting this level of comp probably isn’t a bad idea; especially since we don’t know if he’s fixed his defensive wrestling holes. Mangos is a sick grappler and has okay takedowns of his own but he really struggles with takedown defense. This was an issue JVH gave him in their first fight, and why he came up short on dwcs. His grappling is very good though and he is a great striker as well. He has a particularly nasty head kick and has fast hands as well. I could only find clips of Yanagawa but from the little I saw I think he’s actually really solid. He can do a bit of everything, fights at a high pace, and is fun to watch. I expected him to be a striker with no grappling but his grappling is surprisingly good. He defends takedowns well and has good offensive wrestling of his own. His lone loss is a little fluky as well, he defended a takedown perfectly from the whizzer, but his opponent hit some absurd roll and snatched up an armbar from a crazy position. I couldn’t find Yuito’s full fights but he is solid everywhere and not afraid of a scrap. I did see some flaws in his game though. On the feet he has a lot of power but he is very hittable. He got dropped to one knee and was walking into shots early against Hirata. He was also getting touched up against Kalybek before the KO as well. I don’t think he can stand with Mangos the whole fight here, Mangos is a better striker and can easily KO him here I think. Yanagawa might wrestle here and he can probably get Mangos down, but I think Mangos is the far superior grappler. Yanagawa has good tdd and grappling but when you put him on his back he does struggle. In the Hirata fight he defended really well but in r3 he got put on his back and nearly got finished. Mangos has a very dangerous guard and should he end on top he will likely destroy Yanagawa. This is a really fun scrap and I think Yanagawa is a good fighter himself, however he drew the short straw here as Mangos is a legit talent. His tdd is really bad but he’s so good for only being 22 and only lost to Radley because of some iq mistakes; Radley is very good and Mangos almost beat him even with his horrible tdd.

Ailinuer vs Lim
Lim KO RD 1

This is a really fun fight, I like both of these guys. Ailinuer looks like your typical Chinese NPC fighter on paper but he’s actually pretty skilled; faced a good level of comp, tons of experience, and a pretty well rounded skillset. Lim is an absolute giant at 6”2 and is coming back down to 145 after 4 years in different weight classes. HE recently returned from military service and nuked Yuji, which I find impressive. I guess his level remains to be seen but for the regional scene he’s a top guy. This is a tricky one to pick, Lim is talented but really green, and Ailinuer is a big test. I thin Lim has some special talent though, and is going to be a menace at 145. He was already giant at 155 and coming down 10 pounds I think he’s going to be even harder to deal with. He does have tall mans defense but he also uses his size well, and is very sneaky with his weapons. He’s got a ton of power and isn’t afraid of a scrap. His chin is pretty good and physically he holds up well, usually we see these tall guys struggle but he seems pretty good at this weight class. On the feet I think Lim should have this. Ailinuer is a good striker but nothing special to me. He can compete with Lim but I think he will find it tricky to outpoint him, and I’ve seen Ailinuer dropped before so he will have to be very careful. Ailineur could drop Lim but his chin seems good and Ailinuer doesn’t have a ton of power. The thing that worries me here is the grappling. Ailinuer’s grappling seems bad but for the Chinese scene it’s actually pretty good. He’s fought a lot of Russians/Caucasians (rare to fight them a lot in China) and outwrestled most of them, which was surprising to see. However, I wouldn’t say his wrestling is that good. Yes, he can score takedowns but when on top he doesn’t do a ton, and I've seen him reversed too much for my liking. He gets to his feet well but his game off of his back is not great. I was pretty shocked with Lim’s tdd. He did lose his lone fight to wrestling but not in the way you’d think. He actually got up instantly on every attempt, the issue was that he couldn't separate off the ring and get his game going. That fight also took place in a boxing ring and was at a 164 CW, so there were some outside factors. It wasn’t a bad loss though, he just didn’t do enough. His tdd and defensive grappling is actually pretty good imo. He had defended pretty much everything thats came his way and has not spent much time on his back. He hasn’t panicked when made the nail either, and his back takes are surprisingly good. Ailinuer will wrestle here but I’m honestly not sure it will be that easy. He is a solid wrestler and good everywhere, but Lim seems pretty hard to take down; I think this will be especially true at 145 as well. I like Lim a lot, this may be a little early for him but I think his size and skillset could be a real problem. He’s also very young and already got his military service out of the way, so he can fully focus on MMA. I was impressed with his tdd/getups and with a capable ground game, I think he is going to be a really tricky puzzle to figure out.

Regezhen vs Chagnaanorj
Regezhen KO RD 2

These guys are both pretty mid but both are brawlers so this should hopefully be a fun one. Both are pretty low volume on tape despite the finishes, so I’m hoping they are incentivized like last year. Both of these guys are really underwhelming and it’s a little difficult to get a read on them as their comp is really bad. I like some of Regezhen’s striking but his problem is that he doesn’t throw enough at times. It shouldn't be much of an issue here though, as Dagiisuren throws legitimately nothing. I watched a short highlight vid before going into his full fights and he looked like a monster, but then I quickly realized why the video was so short; he has no highlights because he does nothing in his fights. He’s had some pretty clean knockdowns and had some good finishing sequences in the past but my problem is that he does nothing in the interim. His both losses for example came to the same guy, where they just sparred for 3 rounds and Dagiisuren lost because he didn’t do anything. He played into Bang’s game twice and let him do whatever he wanted. When Dagiisuren lets his hands go he’s got some good power, but his striking is pretty ******. He’s hittable too and often walks right into strikes. In this type of match at range, I think Regezhen should have a sizable advantage. He has similar flaws to Dagiisuren except he actually has good technique and does more. Regezhen has some sick ko’s and has a ton of power in his hands. He also mixes in kicks as well, which will be good here as Dagiisuren is mostly just a boxer. Both these guys have pretty bad ground games but I assume they will just strike with one another. Dagiisuren has a few subs on his record but he doesn’t really proactively look for takedowns. His sub wins have been meme sequences too. I couldn’t find Regezhen’s only loss but since it was gnp to a Russian, I assume he got taken down. He showed some really bad looks on the mat against Maezono but his next fight a few months later he was showing better tdd and awareness, so maybe it was a one off. I still think his grappling is not ufc level but his first layer tdd should be fine here; it may not matter though since Dagiisuren only shoots if his opponents do. Dagiisuren is kind of a nothing burger to me. Idk what to think of Regezhen either but he is lengthy and has good technique. I feel like Dagiisuren is going to play into his game and get bonked at some point.

Aoi vs Song
Song KO RD 1

Glad they brought Song back, he’s really fun. He’s getting a much better matchup this time as well, Aoi will gladly strike with him the entire fight. Song has bad grappling but his striking is really fun. He throws crisp shots straight down the middle and hits really hard. He’s got good cardio too, even in his loss he wasn’t tired, he just couldn’t stop the aggressive takedowns. Aoi is a nothing burger to me. He’s experienced and beat decent comp, but he’s also a low volume striker with not a ton of power. He just sits back at range and puts stuff out there, never really committing to anything nor does he push the pace. I think this is a good fight for Song to not only win, but get a KO. Aoi is going to strike with him and will allow Song to dictate the pace. Aoi is a decnet striker but my problem is that he just kind of exists in there. I think Song will bonk him at some point.

Minami vs Murdoch
Murdoch DEC

These guys both have good records but I think both are pretty low level. Both are really tiny for 135 and don’t have great skillsets. This is a classic striker vs grappler matchup. Minami is a brawler with a bad process and bad defense. He’s got good power for the weight class but everything else about his striking kind of sucks. He can be low volume at times and doesn’t really have a great process either. Sometimes he keeps the pressure high and breaks his opponents and other times he’s sitting back at range not doing much. Minami did win with wrestling in his last fight but he didn’t look overly impressive there; it was more so due to his opponent having no cardio or ground game. While fresh he was getting up pretty easily and Minami was just spamming takedowns. For being a brawler, Minami’s defense is terrible and he doesn’t have a great chin either; he just walks into punches and gets rocked all the time. His fight against the Korean guy he got dropped bad in r1 and the fight prior to that he was getting cooked all of r1 until he randomly bonked him in r2. Murdoch is a really weird choice for RTU; I don’t like them bringing in ANZAC guys as it is, but Murdoch isn’t even entertaining. He looks great on paper with his long winstreak and high finish rate but in reality he is a grindy, boring wrestler who mostly just cage pushes/lay n prays. He is a solid fighter but like, do we really need to see more of him? Literally all he does every fight is pressure you to the cage with overhands, shoot a td, then either cage push or get on top and lay on you until the round is over or you quit. He has a lot of finishes but the majority are all late, and when he’s faced better guys he really struggles to get the finish. His last fight he didn’t come close to anything and even gassed in the last round, and the fight before that he was doing nothing but cage pushing until Kim hurt his knee on a takedown. Murdoch is aggressive to close the distance but his striking is trash, and he gets hit a lot in the process. Minami could hurt him pretty bad here, especially since he thrives in the pocket himself. It’s a really bad look seeing Minami go life and death with everyone on the feet but Murdoch is really hittable and pretty harmless on the feet. I don’t think Minami can stop the lay n pray though. Murdoch doesn’t care about accuracy, if he misses on a td he will continue to cage push until he gets his way. I hate watching this and he is defintely a weasel, but it is effective. It’s also why I dislike putting the ANZAC fighters in RTU, even if flawed they still have a massive advantage with real training and much better MMA scenes than these guys. His wrestling is low level in terms of the UFC but against a Japanese striker, I think he will be able to grind him out. I think its a decision though, unless it turns out Minami is clueless against a real grappler.

Ti vs Tajima
Ti SUB RD 2

I didn’t really look into this one. I didn’t look that hard enough but I could only find Pancrase interviews rather than Ryo’s full fights, and I only found a handful of Ti's fights. Neither of these guys interest me that much so I didn’t bother to look much further than some preliminary research. Ryo seems like a weird choice as his record isn’t pretty nor does he hold many notable wins. He’s got some really bad losses as well, to Kazama and Nakajima. Ti seems like your classic Chinese regional fighter where he’s got a journeyman record and above average skills. One thing I will say though is that he is a big time finisher and is finishing in multiple ways. His comp is also really solid for the Chinese regional scene; almost all of his losses are to the best guys in the scene/guys who made it to the ufc, and he has a plethora of solid wins against actual good fighters for the Chinese scene. He’s also beat up on two ex rtu guys so he is getting experience against international level comp. Again, I didn’t look into this one that much so this is mostly assumptions/wiki capping, but I’ll go with Ti since he trains at the PI and has the better SOS.

Miyaguchi vs Shin
Miyaguchi KO RD 2

Taped both of these guys in depth and still have a hard time getting a read here. Neither are really that good and it’s hard to gauge them because the level of comp is poor as well. Ryuho is a huge BW and explosive striker, but like all cool Japanese kickboxers, he has absolutely no ground game at all. Shin seems really good on paper and is fighting international opponents, but his tape was very underwhelming. This is a classic striker vs grappler matchup, I want to lean the guy who will spam tds and has decent control but idk if his grappling is really that good. Sure, Ryuho can be taken down with little resistance, but holding him there is somewhat difficult. He gets to his feet well and is giant for th weight class which helps. However, he really is a low level grappler and doesn’t know what he’s doing there. For example, last fight he just held the front headlock off of a sprawl and didn’t swing to the back or do anything; he just stalled in sprawl the whole time. You can tell he doesn’t understand the nuances of grappling whatsoever. He is big and dangerous but idk if his striking is really that good either. Sure, he’s giant for the weight class and uses his size decently well, but im not blown away by him. He’s fast and has a nasty southpaw body kick but he does get kind of wild and has tall man’s defense. His process needs some work too; he could’ve ko’ed Ishiihara a few times but got too reckless. He should cruise on the feet here, Shin’s technique is really bad and he doesn’t have a good process either. His footwork is really bad and he’s always out of place when he strikes. He has some okay power but nothing crazy, and much like Ryuho with the grappling, Shin does not understand the nuances of striking. He’s low volume and really clunky, and his style leaves a lot of openings for him to get hit. Shin’s main game is grappling but that’s really un-impressive to me. If he gets on top here I can def see him complicating things but his entries are really poor and he honestly seems kind of weak. His shots are telegraphed and come from far out, and when he gets to the clinch he does not seem that strong. He’s came very close to ending up on bottom a few times but did use the clinch to save him and end up on top. I do like to see that craftiness but its only effective against white belt grapplers. That could work here but I think the size/strength of Ryuho should help him out a good deal here. I’ve seen Shin get taken down himself and reversed many times, so I really doubt the level of his grappling. The first real guy he fought in Bolat was able to take him down with little resistance and tapped him out fairly easily. Ryuho is a very bad grappler with poor tdd but I think he should be strong/wild enough to get to his feet. He also has a big cardio edge here; Shin’s cardio absolutely blows. He is taking deep breaths and has bad body language outside of r1, Ryuho did slow a little against Ishiihara but he was also forcing a wild pace the entire time. Shin looks scared to strike and slows down hard after r1. I think both of these guys are low level but at least Ryuho has some good physical qualities and hits hard, Shin kind of seems fraudulent to me.

Dhant vs Alintozon
Dhant KO RD 1

I’d say this is the lowest level fight out of this episode. Alintozon is really really bad, and is only here because of short notice. Dhant is bad too but he at least has some skills. Dhant is a grappler, his overall game is pretty low level but against Asian competition he is pretty solid. I think his tdd and offensive takedowns are really bad but he has solid control and a good understanding of grappling. When he gets the fight down he immediately starts throwing gnp. His last fight was not the best look but he did show a lot of improvements in his game; he was ripping the southpaw body kick and looking more aggressive than before on the feet, and even though he made errors on the ground he was a step ahead in the wrestling and did a good job of scrambling. I think he will get killed against real comp but against Kimbert he should be more than okay. Kimbert is awful, to put it nicely. He’s fighting very low level comp in the Philippines and isn’t even beating their best guys. The tap I saw of him is super low level: he only throws singular strikes at a time, very hittable, no idea what straight punches are, no real process, and amateurish grappling. His last win was kind of a meme as well, as his opponent got cut and just gave up in the corner. I expect Dhant to score and early takedown and immediately start raining down gnp. His grappling is low level but there definitely have been improvements from his older fights to his newest, and whatever level he’s at currently is clearly much higher than Kimbert, who I don’t think has grappled a day in his life.

[Predictions]

Rongzhu vs. Martinez
Rongzhu, TKO, R1
Evil matchmaking

Xie vs. Cahyadi
Bin Xie, TKO, R1
They must really want Bin Xie in the UFC, this is a non tournament bout that seems specifically made for him to get a highlight reel finish

Mangos vs. Yanagawa
Yuito Yanagawa, TKO, R1
Mangos is a total killer who will always go for the finish but I really love Yanagawa here, he has shown that he has no problem with standing in the fire and his last win was absolutely insane flatline KO over a really good striker

Ailinuer vs. Lim
Ahejiang Ailinuer, SUB, R2
Lim managed to knock out Ephoeviga in his last fight but that mostly seemed like the result of Ephoeviga having a sus chin. Ahejiang is a can crusher but he's seems to know what he's doing on the ground and I think he will be able to take Lim down and submit him

Regezhen vs. Chagnaadorj
Dagiisuren Chagnaadorj, DEC
I seriously doubt either of these guys are winning this tournament. Regezhen just has wins over a bunch of cans and while Chagnaadorj is a bit better and actually fights people with pulses he has been outclassed TWICE by crafty journeyman Jae Hyuk Bang

Aoi vs. Song
Young Jae Song, TKO, R2
I like both of these guys so it's gonna be sad to see someone lose. Aoi has a weird point fighting style that sometimes gets him insane highlight reel knockouts while Song is a total power puncher. When I say that Song is a power puncher I really mean it, he has some serious power in his hands even when he's dead tired from getting wrestled for 3 rounds. I think Song will catch Aoi and finish him

Minami vs. Murdoch
Kasib Murdoch, DEC
This is a fun matchup between undefeated guys who have fought similar level of competition as pros but Murdoch has experience winning against good amateurs

Ti vs. Tajima
Ryo Tajima, TKO, R2
Tajima has actually fought some sneakily good guys while Ti has a record filled with absolute cans

Dhant vs. Alintozon
Rabindra Dhant, TKO, R2
It's hard to tell with the guys from these regions but Dhant actually looks okay. He seems very strong and this should be a pretty easy fight for him

Miyaguchi vs. Koren
Ryuho Miyaguchi, TKO, R1
Koren is somehow one of the best guys in India but will still lose here. He actually had a good first round in his last fight but got destroyed after that. It's not RTU without a Indian guy getting knocked out I guess
